newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian parliament clears BOT airports.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian parliament clears BOT airports.

text.p: The Egyptian parliament has cleared the legislative obstacles to government plans to let the private sector build or operate airports in Egypt.

Under a law passed on Monday night and available on Tuesday, private-sector companies may run airports for up to 99 years under BOT (build, operate and transfer) formulas. At the end of the period, the airports revert to the state.
In practice the government had already put two BOT airport projects out to international tender, on the assumption that it could change the law in time.

The most advanced is that at Marsa Alam on the Red Sea coast, for which the government is negotiating with the Kuwaiti company Mohamed Abdulmuhsin Kharafi and Sons. It is expected to cost about 120 million pounds ($35 million).
In the case of the second airport, at El Alamein on the northwest coast, the Civil Aviation Authority has extended the deadline for bids until January 30.
Other candidates for BOT include desert highways, some power generation plants and some water and sewerage projects.
Earlier this month the Ministry of Housing said it had identified at least 73 projects where the private sector could build and manage water and sewerage services.
The government newspaper al-Ahram said on Tuesday the government would start carrying out a water and sewerage privatisation programme next month.
